A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoA-LoRA work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, despite some internal reporting inconsistencies.

before.justification: v1 reports original GLUE accuracy and training-time measurements, C4 perplexity, zero-shot evaluations and ablation results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds random-extension comparisons, integer-quantization experiments and further model-size and rank evaluations.

M1.justification: Both versions use configuration-conditioned r×r LoRA adjustments, the expected task-loss objective and alternating GP search with segmented Pareto filtering. v2 documents mapper internals and configuration-specific SVD factors; residual SVD already appears in v1 Appendix A.1. These disclosures do not establish an underlying algorithm change.

E1.justification: C4, the four GLUE tasks and the seven zero-shot tasks displayed in Table C.3 are retained. Added backbone sizes, ranks and integer quantization change model settings rather than represented data or task requirements.

E2.justification: Figure 8 adds a random-extension comparator to the existing search/no-search ablation. QLoRA, LQ-LoRA, GPTQ-LoRA and Shared-LoRA remain in their corresponding comparisons; Q-LoRA becoming QLoRA is a naming change.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 extends the stated baseline evaluation grid to include 6 bits, while Table 2 changes baseline solution counts from four to six. Added protocols include integer mixed precision, LLaMA-2-13B at rank 64, additional LLaMA-2-7B ranks and ten randomly added configurations per epoch. However, v2 inconsistently lists five baseline budgets, reports six solutions and retains a four-budget accuracy-gap description.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands the diagnostic evidence: guided search versus random extension, integer-quantization robustness, LLaMA-2-7B rank sensitivity, adapter-similarity analyses across ranks and decoder backbones, and configuration-set size trajectories. Existing unseen-configuration and segment-count analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The additional correlation heatmaps measure adapter similarity, rather than statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Table 2 revises accuracy gaps, HV and baseline runtimes: Shared-LoRA's QNLI HV changes from 0.45 to 0.60 and its gap from -15.93% to +2.90%. Expanded baseline budgets prevent treating these summaries as established same-setting gains. Table C.2 changes GPTQ-LoRA's Qwen2.5-1.5B HV from 0.535 to 0.427, reversing its ranking against CoA-LoRA's unchanged 0.479. Integer-quantization, 13B-model and additional rank results are added; Tables 3 and C.3 retain their values.

T1.justification: Equation 9 swaps the arguments of the nondominance predicate, and Appendix Equation 11 revises the storage constraint into average-bit units. These are localized formal revisions without new theorems or proofs. Algorithm 1 retains the earlier predicate ordering, so the Equation 9 revision is not consistently propagated.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions remain unchanged. The introduction and conclusion narrow the reported accuracy-gain range from 2.36%-10.37% to 1.74%-8.89%; the conclusion also revises HV improvements over LQ-LoRA from 3%-8% to 2%-7%.

C2.justification: New discussion attributes guided search's advantage to candidate quality after comparison with random extension. Added integer, larger-model and rank results are interpreted as broader applicability and low-bit stability. The rationale for NormalFloat changes from blockwise expressiveness to preservation of small-magnitude weights.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.1 specifies seven 8-dimensional embeddings, a two-layer MLP with hidden dimension 128, LayerNorm, SiLU, learnable output scaling and parameter counts. v2 also clarifies configuration-specific SVD construction, discloses layerwise baseline configuration assignment, provides explicit bit accounting and adds an implementation-repository link. These substantially improve documentation of previously unspecified implementation choices.

R1.justification: New Section 2.3 substantially expands positioning against parameter and LoRA generation, discussing P-diff, G.pt, CONDP-DIFF, ICM-LoRA and LoRA-Gen and their reliance on trained parameters or expert adapters. The quantization discussion and citations are also revised, including LowRA; the GPT3.int8 and SmoothQuant references are removed.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative sequence are retained. Changes include localized NormalFloat explanations, clearer C/Q terminology, baseline-name standardization, additional related-work and appendix subsections, and publication-header, corresponding-author and acknowledgment additions.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4, A.1, C.4 and C.5, expands the similarity heatmaps, adds a configuration-size plot and introduces a third curve in Figure 8. Figures 2-3 are redrawn or relabeled, plot axes are clarified as average bits, and numerous displays are relocated. Existing zero-shot and RoBERTa rank results remain identifiable.

improvement.justification: v1 leaves the central mapper architecture largely unspecified and compares configuration search only with no search. v2 supplies concrete implementation details and tests guided search against random expansion, substantially strengthening reproducibility and evidence for the central mechanism. Integer-quantization and larger-model/rank tests further support applicability. Inconsistent baseline bit counts and incomplete propagation of the Pareto correction limit some comparisons, but the implementation and experimental gains provide a substantial net improvement.
